extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news organizations, and potential entrants to the George Polk Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and descriptive criteria used by Long Island University to recognize and select winners of the George Polk Awards (and the Sydney Schanberg Prize) across many journalism categories, emphasizing investigative and enterprising reporting. Covers award-level purposes, category-specific qualities illustrated by winning entries, and procedural notes about selection and submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative and enterprising reporting that gains attention and achieves results
rubrics_metrics.description: The awards place a premium on investigative and enterprising reporting that gains attention and achieves results; they honor special achievement in print, online, or broadcast journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General mission statement for the George Polk Awards: preference for work that uncovers important information, attracts public attention, and leads to tangible consequences or reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2025 recipients were selected by a panel of journalists and educators from 492 entries submitted by news organizations and individuals or recommended by former winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural note: winners are chosen by a professional panel reviewing submitted or recommended entries; implies ability to compete within a large, peer-reviewed pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Award — pioneering career achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: Career Award presented to pioneering journalists in recognition of a distinguished career (example: Maria Hinojosa, anchor and executive producer of Latino USA and founder of Futuro Media).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes long-term, pioneering contributions to journalism rather than a single story; intended for individuals with sustained impact and leadership in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Reporting — investigative, risky reporting exposing wrongdoing
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign Reporting goes to groundbreaking investigative accounts, reported at considerable risk, revealing how well-placed individuals profited from trafficking or other abuses (example: reporting that revealed exploitation of East African women recruited for domestic work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values reporting from abroad that uncovers systemic abuses, often done under personal risk and producing original revelations about corruption, trafficking, exploitation, or other harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Reporting — exposing policy decisions and global impact
rubrics_metrics.description: International Reporting awarded for stories exposing cavalier approaches by officials in dismantling institutions (example: reporting on the U.S. Agency for International Development and the harm an aid cutoff had on millions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewards investigative work that links policy decisions to large-scale humanitarian or global impacts, using documentation and reporting to demonstrate harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Reporting — relentless watchdog coverage of power and norms
rubrics_metrics.description: National Reporting recognizes relentless and unflinching coverage of a White House that defied standards and norms in expanding executive power and other abuses (example: coverage documenting abuses of presidential power and misleading the public).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values persistent watchdog journalism that exposes institutional and governmental abuses, holds power accountable, and documents systemic failures over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Reporting — probing civil liberties and institutional overreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Local Reporting cited for probing cases that reveal civil liberties consequences of local/academic policing actions (example: investigation of a Turkish graduate student's arrest and transfer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewards local investigations that uncover abuses affecting individuals in local communities and that illuminate broader policy or civil-rights concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice Reporting — exposing institutional violence and prompting reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice Reporting honored for exposing the beating death of an inmate by prison guards, establishing patterns of similar deaths and portraying a prison system so out of control that video evidence of torture was ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values investigative work that documents specific abuses, establishes patterns or systemic problems, and contributes to legislative or policy change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Reporting — thoroughly researched reporting on community impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental Reporting awarded to a thoroughly researched series highlighting the strain new data centers place on communities by diverting power, water, and economic support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewards deep reporting that combines research and local impact analysis to show environmental and community consequences of corporate or infrastructural projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health Reporting — use of data, human stories, and historical context
rubrics_metrics.description: Health Reporting honored work chronicling degradation of the FDA and a 10-part series 'American Science, Shattered,' using data, human stories and historical context to document the impact of federal disruption of scientific research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values reporting that combines quantitative analysis, individual narratives, and institutional history to document harms in public health and science oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political Reporting — meticulous, explanatory reporting on power brokers
rubrics_metrics.description: Political Reporting recognizes meticulously researched pieces depicting influential technocrats or power brokers behind government decisions (example: profile of the 'Shadow President' directing budget and policy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewards in-depth profiles and explanatory pieces that reveal the influence of unelected officials and the mechanics of political power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magazine Reporting — long-form, exhaustive investigations linking causes and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Magazine Reporting awarded for multi-year, exhaustive reporting showing how tragedies (e.g., migrant deaths) resulted from smuggling operations and policy choices, and profiling survivors to reveal deeper systems at work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values long-form narrative investigations that combine deep reporting over time with human stories and structural analysis to connect individual tragedies to broader systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immigration Reporting — spotlighting wrongful deportation and systemic errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Immigration Reporting recognizes work that spotlights wrongful deportation cases that highlight administrative error and systemic injustice (example: publicizing a case of a deported man despite protected status).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewards reporting that uncovers individual cases emblematic of systemic immigration failures and brings attention to bureaucratic or legal errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photojournalism — powerful visual storytelling produced under extreme conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Photojournalism award recognizes images produced under extremely difficult conditions with limited access, constant danger and scarce supplies, portraying human anguish and exposing famine or suffering (examples: images from Gaza and immigrants facing deportation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values courage, access, and the ability to convey human suffering and complex situations visually, often under personal risk and constrained resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Television Reporting — investigative broadcast exposing official narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: National Television Reporting awarded for broadcast segments that refute official assertions (example: proving most deported Venezuelans were not violent felons and profiling innocent detainees), using internal documents and on-the-ground reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewards television journalism that uses documentary evidence and reporting to challenge official narratives and humanize affected people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Television Reporting — documentary coverage of frontline conflict with vivid, immersive footage
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign Television Reporting goes to documentary features that bring home the harrowing nature of front-line warfare using bodycam and drone footage and close accompaniment of soldiers (example: '2000 Meters to Andriivka').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values immersive, cinematic reporting from conflict zones that conveys the reality of combat, often using novel or risky filming methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sydney Schanberg Prize — long-form investigative/enterprise journalism criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Schanberg Prize honors long-form investigative or enterprise journalism embodying qualities reflected in Schanberg’s career: 'highly distinguished, deep coverage of armed conflicts; local, state or federal government corruption; military injustice; war crimes, genocide or sedition; or authoritarian government abuses' of at least 5,000 words 'that results from staying with a story, sometimes at great risk or sacrifice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit eligibility and qualitative standards: long-form (≥5,000 words), deep and distinguished coverage on specified topics, produced through sustained commitment and sometimes personal risk; comes with a $25,000 award and is intended to honor reporting in Schanberg's tradition.
